# Definition

The Service Hub is a multi-component platform designed to provide ecosystems with a comprehensive toolbox to support the implementation of an integrated approach to the **Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle (RRR)** of consumer-used **Electrical and Electronic Equipment (EEE)**. All these components need to work together to provide an intuitive experience for users by integrating all tools into a customer journey.

These tools need to work individually as well and ultimately must be able to be integrated into custom workflows within the different ecosystems. The tools must therefore be designed with a single point of contact in mind. This singe point of contact is an API that other systems can call to get the functionality of each specific tool.

The platform is designed as a collection of modular components, each exposing its functionality through standardized APIs. While each component can operate independently, all components are architected to work together seamlessly within a unified customer journey. This ensures a consistent and intuitive user experience across the ecosystem.

To enable flexibility and interoperability, the Service Hub follows a **single point of contact principle**. All tools are accessible through a centralized API layer, which acts as the primary integration interface for external systems. Through this API layer, third-party applications and ecosystem partners can:

- Access individual tool functionalities
- Integrate tools into end-to-end customer journeys
- Embed specific capabilities into custom workflows
- Retrieve, update, and manage data across components

In addition to serving as a functional integration layer, the platform operates as a developer-oriented API registry and discovery environment. Developers can register their APIs, publish documentation, and make their services searchable and reusable within the ecosystem.

By centralizing access, standardizing integration, and improving discoverability, the Service Hub enhances API visibility, promotes reuse, reduces duplication of development efforts, and accelerates the deployment of high-quality digital services across participating ecosystems.

# Objectives

The Service Hub is designed as a federated collection of software tools and APIs developed and maintained by multiple organizations. Given that each tool follows its own support model, lifecycle, and upgrade path, this deliverable aims to define the principles, standards, and technical mechanisms required to enable effective integration and long-term sustainability of the platform.

The primary objectives of the Service Hub are as follows:

## Provide a Centralized API Registry

Establish a centralized registry that serves as the authoritative catalogue of all available tools and APIs within the Service Hub ecosystem. This registry will function as the single point of reference for discovering, accessing, and managing integrations.

## Enable API Publication and Lifecycle Management

Allow developers and contributing organizations to:

- Register new APIs and tools
- Publish and maintain API metadata
- Provide and update technical documentation
- Manage versioning and lifecycle information

The platform must support future extensibility, ensuring that new APIs can be registered or existing APIs updated at a later stage without disrupting existing integrations.

## Support Technical Integration into Custom Workflows

Provide comprehensive technical guidance, standards, and interface definitions to enable companies to integrate individual tools into their own systems and workflows.

As integration requires technical expertise, this document primarily addresses architects, developers, and system integrators.

Organizations with limited technical capabilities may alternatively access the tools through either the publicly available Service Hub website or the predefined customer journeys that combine multiple tools into a guided experience.

## Enable Discovery and Searchability

Provide robust search and filtering capabilities that allow users to discover tools based on:

- Functional capabilities
- Technology stack or integration standards
- Relevant use cases

This ensures efficient identification of appropriate tools and reduces duplication of development effort.

## Promote Standardization and Best Practices

Encourage consistent API documentation, standardized metadata structures, and adoption of integration best practices. This improves interoperability, usability, and long-term maintainability across the ecosystem.

## Support Ecosystem Growth and Reuse

Facilitate the development of a scalable and sustainable ecosystem of reusable software components. By improving visibility, documentation quality, and integration simplicity, the Service Hub accelerates adoption and collaboration between participating organizations.

# Features

## User Registration & Authentication

The platform provides secure identity and access management to ensure controlled participation and clear ownership of APIs and tools. As the service hub has already implemented an authentication and authorization, this can be reused.

Registration is only necessary for adding or changing content. This ensures that editing, publishing, and administrative actions are restricted to authorized roles. Reading or searching for content is freely available for all.

## API & Tool Registration

The system enables structured onboarding and lifecycle management of APIs and software tools. The system must at least be able to submit new tools, update existing tools or metadata and to publish new versions. It should also be possible to deprecate outdated or unsupported tools while maintaining traceability.

This ensures transparency, maintainability, and long-term governance of the API ecosystem.

## Documentation Management

Comprehensive documentation support ensures APIs are understandable, accessible, and easy to integrate. The ability to upload files or link to external documentation sources is essential for developers to be able to use the API's. The documentation should include API reference documentation, examples, integration guides and code snippets.

These capabilities reduce integration time and improve developer experience.

## Search & Discovery

To maximize reuse and visibility, the platform includes advanced discovery functionality. A good searchable index promotes reuse and prevents duplication of functionality.

# Architecture and database

## System Architecture Overview

The Service Hub is built on a **microservices architecture** in which an API Gateway (NestJS, port 3000) acts as the single HTTP entry point. Each capability is an independent service communicating with the Gateway over an internal TCP message bus. All services share a common **PostgreSQL 14** database, with each service managing its own schema via TypeORM. Elasticsearch powers full-text search for devices and repairers; logs are aggregated via Fluentd and visualized in Kibana.

| Service | Port | Role |
|---|---|---|
| **api-gateway** | 3000 | HTTP entry point, authentication, OpenAPI documentation |
| **user-management** | 3001 | User accounts, roles, permissions |
| **repairers-service** | 3002 | Repairer directory and geolocation search |
| **devices-service** | 3003 | Device catalog, categories, technical specifications |
| **notifications-service** | 3004 | Email and SMS delivery |
| **ownership-service** | 3005 | User–device ownership relationships |
| **oauth-service** | 3006 | OAuth 2.0 tokens, OIDC, refresh token rotation |
| **fast-plan-eco-service** | 3007 | Eco-route planning, geocoding, GPX export |
| **external-adapters-service** | 3008 | iFixit (repair guides) and Fixometer (environmental impact) adapters |
| **surveys-service** | 3009 | Survey creation and response collection |
| **api-catalog-service** | 3011 | **Tool registry and discovery — core of this deliverable** |
| **spare-parts-service** | 3012 | Spare parts search |
| **device-identification** | 8000 | ML-based device classification (Python) |

## The API Catalog Service

The **api-catalog-service** is the direct implementation of the Tool Database concept. It stores a structured registry of external APIs and tools that ecosystem partners can discover and integrate. Every entry follows a three-stage moderation lifecycle: a user with the `api_catalog.submit` permission submits a tool (status: `PENDING`); an administrator with `api_catalog.admin` approves or rejects it; once approved, the entry becomes publicly visible without authentication. Platform-native tools are pre-seeded at deployment via an `isBuiltIn` flag.

## Data Model

Each tool is stored as a single record in the `api_tools` table, with fields organized into six groups:

| Group | Key fields |
|---|---|
| **Basic information** | `name`, `shortDescription`, `fullDescription`, `websiteUrl`, `baseApiUrl`, `category` (`RECYCLING`, `REPAIR`, `DIAGNOSIS`, `SPARE_PARTS`, `CERTIFICATION`, `OTHER`), `tags` |
| **Access and authentication** | `isPubliclyAccessible`, `requiresAccount`, `requiresApiKey`, `authType` (`NONE`, `API_KEY`, `OAUTH2`, `BASIC_AUTH`, `JWT`, `OTHER`), `authDetails` |
| **Pricing** | `pricingModel` (`FREE`, `FREEMIUM`, `PAID`, `OPEN_SOURCE`, `UNKNOWN`), `pricingDetails`, `pricingUrl` |
| **Documentation** | `documentationUrl`, `swaggerUrl`, `openApiSpecUrl`, `apiVersion`, `supportedFormats` (`JSON`, `XML`, `CSV`, `GRAPHQL`, `RSS`), `endpoints` |
| **Moderation** | `status` (`PENDING`, `APPROVED`, `REJECTED`), `rejectionReason`, `submitterUserId`, `approvedBy`, `approvedAt`, `isBuiltIn` |
| **Audit** | `createdAt`, `updatedAt` |

## Authentication and Access Control

Authentication is handled at the API Gateway level using two mechanisms: **JWT Bearer tokens** (issued after email/password login, valid one hour) and **OAuth 2.0** (authorization code with PKCE for user-facing apps; client credentials for machine-to-machine). Social login via Google and Facebook is also supported. Access to the catalog is governed by permissions: reading the public catalog requires no authentication; submitting a tool requires `api_catalog.submit`; moderating submissions requires `api_catalog.admin`.

## Search and Discovery

The catalog supports filtering by category, authentication type, pricing model, and moderation status, with results sorted by creation date. Full-text search across names, descriptions, and tags is a planned extension, leveraging the Elasticsearch infrastructure already in place for the device and repairer catalogs.

# Benefits

The implementation of a centralized, API-first Service Hub delivers strategic, operational, and technical advantages for ecosystem participants. By consolidating tools, documentation, and discovery mechanisms into a single platform, the system enhances efficiency, transparency, and collaboration.

## Faster Developer Onboarding and Tool Adoption

The platform significantly reduces the time required for developers to discover, understand, and integrate APIs by:

- Centralized access to tools and documentation
- Standardized API descriptions and metadata
- Clear authentication and integration guidelines

This lowers entry barriers for new participants and accelerates ecosystem growth.

## Increased Reuse of Existing APIs and Services

By making APIs searchable, well-documented, and categorized, the platform promotes reuse over redevelopment.

Organizations can build on existing capabilities instead of reinventing similar solutions.

## Stronger Collaboration Within the Developer Community

The platform fosters transparency and shared ownership across ecosystem stakeholders. This is provided by:

- Clearly defined API ownership and contribution roles
- Shared visibility into available tools and updates
- Easier communication between tool providers and consumers

This collaborative environment strengthens trust and continuous improvement.

## Improved Governance and Lifecycle Management

Centralized registration and versioning improve long-term sustainability. By providing a controlled deprecation processes and a clear version history, users get a better oversight of ecosystem-wide capabilities.

This ensures the ecosystem remains maintainable, secure, and scalable over time.

## Enhanced Integration Flexibility

The API-first design allows tools to function independently while remaining interoperable. This ensures:

- Seamless integration into predefined customer journeys
- Embedding into custom workflows
- Compatibility with diverse external systems
- Scalable expansion with new tools and services

This flexibility allows ecosystems to adapt the platform to evolving operational needs.

# Conclusion

This system will serve as a **single source of truth for developer tools**, enabling efficient discovery, reliable documentation, and long-term ecosystem growth. By lowering the barrier to finding and integrating APIs, the platform will significantly enhance developer productivity and innovation.
